| D-26.1 | §26.1 | HIST | **Internal:** `Logger` handle (owned ident, explicit facility), with an optional structured journald protocol. **Boundary:** the global logger keeps the ident *by pointer*, as the contract says. The connection is synchronised (observable, stricter). |
| D-26.2 | §26.1 | HIST, ARB | **syslog (phase 13); decisions.** `liella::log::Logger` (owned ident, options, facility, mask, channels); the global logger `legacy::log_compat::GLOBAL` keeps the ident by pointer under one lock over settings, connection and delivery; a fork child resets the lock and shares the connection. **Never blocks indefinitely:** sends use `MSG_DONTWAIT\|MSG_NOSIGNAL` and `ppoll` with at most 1 s per message, and the console is opened `O_NONBLOCK` with the same bound (the reference blocks on a full receiver or a FIFO console with no reader); a timeout counts as not delivered (`LOG_CONS` then writes to the console). One reconnect and resend on any other failure. The socket is moved to descriptor 3 or above. The stream transport cuts the text at the first NUL. `errno` is never changed (X3; the reference leaks it after a failed send). A NULL format logs nothing (the reference crashes). Kept from the reference: the extra "unknown facility/priority" record for stray priority bits, `openlog` replacing the options, facility 0 accepted, `closelog` resetting only the ident, `setlogmask(0)` querying; timestamp per `localtime_r`, English month names; console form `IDENT[PID]: MSG\r\n`. The journald protocol of D-26.1 is not built (optional). `openlog(NULL)` selects the program name, also after an earlier `openlog` with another ident (openlog(3); owner ruling 2026-10-04; the reference keeps the previous ident: recorded in `syslog_products`). |

| D-27.2 | §27.1 | HIST | **Internal:** `Result`. **Boundary:** per-thread `dlerror` state. |

| D-27.4 | §27 | — | **`dl_iterate_phdr`** (static programs, until the loader of phase 14 supplies the object list): one callback for the main program (name "", `AT_PHDR`/`AT_PHNUM`, `dlpi_addr` from `PT_PHDR`, TLS module 1 and the calling thread's block when `PT_TLS` exists), then one for the vDSO (`linux-vdso.so.1`, ELF64 header fields e_phoff at 32, e_phentsize 54, e_phnum 56) when `AT_SYSINFO_EHDR` is set, as a glibc static program reports (probe); `dlpi_adds` = objects, `dlpi_subs` = 0, `size` = 64; a non-zero callback result stops the walk and is returned; it reads immutable startup data only (async-signal-safe). **`stime`** is compat-only as in glibc 2.39: `libc.so` exports `stime@GLIBC_2.2.5` (non-default; `.symver` stub in `s23_time.rs`, listed in the version script by `cargo xtask so`), `libc.a` offers no plain `stime`, so no new program links it while old binaries resolve it. Known difference: `libc.so` binds `dl_iterate_phdr` GLOBAL where glibc binds WEAK (the same for every WEAK export, e.g. `fgetc`). Probes: CONF-SYMS-2. |
| D-27.5 | §27.1 | — | **`_dl_find_object`** (static programs, until phase 14): a `pc` in one of the main program's `PT_LOAD` segments gives that segment's range (a static glibc 2.39 program reports the segment, not the whole object), one in the vDSO the vDSO's whole mapped range; `dlfo_eh_frame` = the object's `PT_GNU_EH_FRAME` address (0 without one), `dlfo_flags` 0, result 0; any other `pc` (stack, past `_end`, 0) gives -1 and leaves `*result` alone. libgcc_eh (GCC 13) calls it, so a static C++ or `-fexceptions` program needs it to link. Exported with feature `runtime` only (`export! { runtime ... }`): the answer covers only a process Liella started, so test builds that interpose exports on a host process keep the host's (interposed, it hid the host's shared objects from Rust's panic unwinder: SIGABRT). Known gap: `dlfo_link_map` is 0 (no `struct link_map` before phase 14; glibc gives a non-null one). Probe: PTHREAD-ONCE-UNWIND-2 (static and dynamic glibc). |
| D-27.6 | §27.5 | — | **`__x86_get_cpuid_feature_leaf@GLIBC_2.33`** (`<sys/platform/x86.h>`, behind `CPU_FEATURE_PRESENT`/`CPU_FEATURE_ACTIVE`): returns `struct cpuid_feature` (32 bytes, align 4: the raw CPUID words eax, ebx, ecx, edx, then the "active" words in that order). Index to leaf: 0=1, 1=7.0, 2=0x80000001, 3=0xd.1, 4=0x80000007, 5=0x80000008, 6=7.1, 7=0x19, 8=0x14.0, 9=0x24. A leaf or subleaf past the CPU's maximum reads zero. Index 10 and above (including 0xffffffff) gets one shared all-zero entry, never NULL. The table is filled on the first call (`liella_rt::cpu::feature_leaves`). Active = present AND a fixed per-bit rule: the `ACTIVE_ALWAYS` bits; FMA/AVX/F16C/AVX2 only with XCR0 SSE+AVX state; AVX-512 F/DQ/CD/BW/VL only with XCR0 0xe6; HLE/RTM inactive and RTM_ALWAYS_ABORT active (even though not present) when 7.EDX bit 11 or 13 is set. Probe: X86-CPUID-FEATURE-LEAF (glibc 2.39 on Skylake-SP host Skylake-SP, Haswell-EP host Haswell, Broadwell-EP host Broadwell, Zen 1 host). **Known gaps (ruling #778, #781, #782):** (1) an active bit never seen present on a probed CPU stays inactive (AVX512_IFMA/VBMI/VNNI/BITALG, GFNI, VAES, VPCLMULQDQ, the 7.1, 0x19, 0x14 and 0x24 active bits, among others). This is the safe answer: a feature is never claimed usable when it is not. Trigger: extend `ACTIVE_ALWAYS` once a newer CPU (Ice Lake+ / Zen 4) can be probed against glibc. (2) The TSX rule (abort bit 11 or 13) rests on one CPU per side (Skylake-SP host with bit 13, Broadwell-EP host without either bit). A model-based rule cannot be told apart on these hosts. (3) `glibc.cpu.hwcaps` tunable masking of the active bits is not implemented. |
| D-27.7 | §27 | SEC | **The loader's ELF reader (`liella_ld::elf`, IP-24 part 1, DL-ELF-READ-1): error rules.** Input is a byte slice; no I/O, no allocation, no panic, no read outside the slice; every offset, count and size is checked with checked arithmetic (threat-model rule 4). `Elf::parse::<A: Arch>` checks, in this order, and returns the first failure as a typed `ElfError`: length >= 64 (`TooShort`); magic; `EI_CLASS` = `A::EI_CLASS` = ELFCLASS64 (`WrongClass`, s27_1_f_0); `EI_DATA` = `A::EI_DATA` (`WrongData`; fields are decoded in that byte order); `EI_VERSION` = 1; `EI_OSABI` System V or GNU; `e_type` `ET_EXEC` or `ET_DYN`; `e_machine` = `A::E_MACHINE` (identity only through `liella_ld::arch`, design §0a); `e_version` = 1; `e_ehsize` = 64; `e_phnum` != `PN_XNUM` (section headers are never read); `e_phentsize` = 56 unless `e_phnum` = 0; the program header table inside the slice and not overlapping the ELF header; then per program header in index order: `p_offset + p_filesz` and `p_vaddr + p_memsz` do not overflow, `p_align` 0 or a power of two, `PT_LOAD` `p_filesz <= p_memsz`, the file ranges of `PT_DYNAMIC`/`PT_INTERP`/`PT_NOTE` overlap neither the ELF header nor the table, at most one `PT_DYNAMIC` and one `PT_INTERP`. Segment contents are checked when read (the slice may be a file prefix): a range outside the slice is `OutOfRange`; `PT_INTERP` is a non-empty path with exactly one NUL, at the end; `PT_DYNAMIC` is a multiple of 16 bytes and holds a `DT_NULL` (entries after the first `DT_NULL` are never read); `DT_STRTAB` and `DT_STRSZ` at most once each, both or neither, and both when a string-valued tag (`DT_NEEDED`, `DT_SONAME`, `DT_RPATH`, `DT_RUNPATH`) is present; the string table lies wholly in the file-backed part of one `PT_LOAD` (`AddressNotMapped`); a string offset is below `DT_STRSZ` and its NUL inside the table. Notes are padded to 8 when `p_align` is 8 and to 4 when it is 0-4 (any other value is `BadNoteAlign`); a note header, name or descriptor past the segment end is `NoteTruncated`, a non-empty name without a final NUL `BadNoteName`; `NT_GNU_PROPERTY_TYPE_0` properties are 8-aligned and a property past its descriptor is `PropertyTruncated`. Iterators yield `Result` and stop after the first error. Semantic segment checks (order, congruence, overlap of `PT_LOAD`s) belong to the mapper (§3); dlerror texts wait for the M14-0/DL-0b probes. Tests: `crates/ld/tests/elf_reader.rs` (malformed corpus), `elf_readelf_parity.rs` (readelf -h/-l/-d/-n). |
| D-27.8 | §27 | SEC | **The loader's ELF reader, part 2 (`liella_ld::elf`, IP-24 part 2, DL-ELF-READ-2): hash tables, versions, relocation iterators.** Same input rules as D-27.7 (no I/O, allocation, panic or read outside the slice; checked arithmetic; iterators yield one error and stop). Tables are found through `Dynamic`: a part-2 tag occurs at most once (`DuplicateDynamic`); address/size pairs (`DT_RELA`/`RELASZ`, `DT_JMPREL`/`PLTRELSZ`, `DT_RELR`/`RELRSZ`, `DT_VERDEF`/`VERDEFNUM`, `DT_VERNEED`/`VERNEEDNUM`) are both or neither (`MissingDynamic(tag)`); `DT_RELAENT` = 24 and `DT_RELRENT` = 8 are required with `DT_RELA`/`DT_RELR`, `DT_PLTREL` = `DT_RELA` with `DT_JMPREL` (`MissingDynamic`/`BadDynamicValue`); a size that is not whole entries is `TableSize`. Fixed-length tables (SysV hash header + `nbucket+nchain` words, GNU hash header + Bloom words + buckets, RELA, RELR) lie wholly in the file-backed part of one `PT_LOAD` (`AddressNotMapped`); tables walked to their end (GNU chain, verdef, verneed, versym) are read within the rest of that segment. GNU hash: at least one Bloom word and a shift below 64 (`BadHashHeader`); a bucket below `symoffset` or a chain past the mapped bytes is `HashIndex`. SysV: a bucket/chain value at or past `nchain` is `HashIndex`, a chain longer than `nchain` `HashChainLoop`; no buckets = empty. Symbol count: SysV `nchain`, else the end of the GNU chain from the highest bucket (all buckets empty: `symoffset`, a lower bound). Versions: revision 1 (`BadVersionRevision`); a chain ending (next 0) before its count is `VersionCount`, an entry past the segment `VersionTruncated`; names through the string rules of D-27.7; a `versym` index above the highest `vd_ndx`/`vna_other` (hidden bit masked) is `VersionIndex`, an entry past the mapping `SymbolIndex` (the count is a hint, not a bound). RELA entries are classified only through `Arch::classify` into `RelocKind`; an unknown type is `Unsupported(n)` and still yielded (design §0a); `TextRel` carries width, pc-relative and signed (32 vs 32S). RELR: an even entry is an address, an odd entry a 63-word bitmap after the previous address or bitmap; a bitmap with no address before it is `RelrNoBase`, an address past 2^64 `RelrOverflow`. Tests: `crates/ld/tests/elf_tables.rs`, `elf_readelf_parity.rs` (readelf -r/-V/--dyn-syms); fuzz target `elf` (docs/fuzzing.md). |
| D-27.9 | §22, §27 | — | **The placeholder libraries (DL-1 `DL-PLACEHOLDERS`, design §16, R14-12).** `cargo xtask so` builds `libpthread.so.0`, `libdl.so.2`, `librt.so.1`, `libutil.so.1`, `libanl.so.1` and `libc_malloc_debug.so.0` from `spec/abi/versions.tsv` (`xtask/src/placeholders.rs`), each with its soname and `DT_NEEDED libc.so.6`. **Rule:** a library's version nodes are the versions of its rows (numeric order, each the parent of the next, no `GLIBC_PRIVATE`); it exports each of its rows whose name `libc.so.6` has no row for, at the row's version and binding; every other name is reached through `libc.so.6` and never defined twice. So the five placeholders export only their `__lib<x>_version_placeholder` versions (bodies return), and `libc_malloc_debug.so.0` only `malloc_get_state`/`malloc_set_state` (bodies in `crates/libc-so/placeholders/libc_malloc_debug.c`: NULL / -1 with `ENOSYS`, as `libc.a`'s, D-3.5) while defining all its nodes; preloading it gives no hooks. An export without a body is a build error. Empty `libdl.a`, `librt.a`, `libutil.a`, `libanl.a` (and `libpthread.a`) let `-static -l<x>` resolve. **Check:** each built library is read back with `readelf` and compared with the table independently of the generator (soname, `DT_NEEDED`, version definitions, every defined export: unversioned, another library's row, a `libc.so.6` name, a missing row are errors), and no shared product (`libc.so.6`, `libm.so.6` included) defines or exports `GLIBC_PRIVATE` (R14-12). Tests: `placeholders::tests` (xtask), `s22_n_1` (links `-lpthread -ldl -lrt -lutil -lanl` statically and runs; dynamically, links only until DL-14). |
| D-27.10 | §1.1, §27 | SEC | **The self-relocator** (DL-BOOT-RELOC, phase 14 DL-4, ruling R14-1 option (a), design §1): logic in `liella_ld::boot` (pure, host-tested), memory views in `boundary/src/bootstrap.rs` (category *slice*). First user: the static-PIE start of `libc.a` (closes phase-4 deviation 2); `ld.so` reuses it (DL-5). Rules: (1) the image is found through its own ELF header, `__ehdr_start` declared hidden and NOT weak in a C file of its own (`csys/src/adapter/image_anchor.c`, helper `liella_link_image_header`), so the compiler takes its address with one RIP-relative instruction; every reference made before pass 1 ends must be PC-relative like this (a weak reference compiles to a GOT load, and the GOT is unrelocated: DL-BOOT-RELOC's first `_DYNAMIC` anchor crashed every static PIE). `cargo xtask so` checks that the anchor's archive member references `__ehdr_start` and has no GOT-typed relocation. A static PIE links the start object `liella-rcrt1.o` (`entry.S` assembled with `-DLIELLA_STATIC_PIE`; its `_start` calls `liella_start_main_static_pie`, PC-relative, checked by `cargo xtask so`), which runs `runtime::start::<true>`; `liella-crt1.o` runs `start::<false>`, which compiles no relocation step and no type test (DL-BOOT-RELOC-3: no static non-PIE start pays for static PIE). The relocating start still relocates only when the header's `e_type` is `ET_DYN`; bias = the header's run-time address minus the `p_vaddr` of the `PT_LOAD` at file offset 0, and `PT_DYNAMIC` is found at bias + its `p_vaddr` (a static PIE from GNU ld has no `PT_PHDR`, so the header bias reads 0; the TLS image and RELRO range are moved by the real bias). (2) It needs one `PT_DYNAMIC` and exactly one writable `PT_LOAD`; every target lies in that segment (8 bytes inside it), every table (`DT_RELA`, `DT_JMPREL`, `DT_RELR`) holds whole entries and lies outside it; `DT_TEXTREL`, `DT_RELAENT` not 24, `DT_RELRENT` not 8, `DT_PLTREL` not `DT_RELA`, a missing `DT_NULL`, a RELR bitmap before an address or an address overflow are refused. (3) Pass 1, before any relocated data is read: `DT_RELA` then `DT_JMPREL` entries of kind `RelocKind::Relative` (through `Arch::classify`, never a raw type number) get bias + addend, then each RELR address gets += bias; `Irelative` and `None` wait; any other kind is refused. A refusal in pass 1 writes one fixed line to fd 2 and exits 127 (nothing that reads relocated data may run). (4) Pass 2, where the non-PIE start applies `.rela.iplt` (after the CPU paths, before the constructors and before RELRO is protected): each `Irelative` entry of both tables calls its resolver at bias + addend and stores the result; the segment view is made after the resolver returns. No panics anywhere in the relocator (a `Location` is relocated data). (5) `xtask so` makes `DW.ref.rust_eh_personality` weak hidden in the product crate's own `libc.a` objects (it was LOCAL in a COMDAT group, so a PIE link refused the other members' references). Tests: `liella_ld::boot` unit tests; `conformance/c/s01_static_pie.c` (RELR) and `s01_static_pie_rela.c` (RELA), each with an IFUNC called and taken by address, a pointer in the TLS image, a constructor and 100 starts (50 randomised, 50 `ADDR_NO_RANDOMIZE`); plants `handoff/DL-BOOT-RELOC-plants.txt`. (Amended by D-27.25.) |
| D-27.11 | §27.1 | — | **Symbol lookup (`liella_ld::symbols`, phase 14 DL-9, DL-SYMBOLS).** Pure logic over the reader (no I/O, allocation or panic; malformed tables give a typed `LookupError`). The reader gains `Dynamic::symtab` (`DT_SYMENT`, when present, must be 24; an index at or past the hash-table symbol count is `SymbolIndex`). **Hashes:** gABI SysV hash and the GNU hash (`h*33+c` from 5381); an object is searched through its GNU table when it has one (Bloom check, then chain entries whose hash matches with bit 0 ignored), else SysV; both give the same answers. **Definitions:** defined (`st_shndx` not `SHN_UNDEF`), binding GLOBAL/WEAK/GNU_UNIQUE, type NOTYPE/OBJECT/FUNC/COMMON/TLS/GNU_IFUNC, visibility not HIDDEN/INTERNAL, versym index not 0. **Versions** (probe-settled, spec/behaviour/dynlink.md "Symbol binding"): an unversioned relocation reference (versym 0/1 or no versym) binds the definition with the lowest version index, hidden or not (base first, then the oldest version); a lookup by name alone (`dlsym`) binds base or default (not hidden) definitions only; a named version (`vna_other` resolved to its name, `dlvsym`) binds exactly that version, hidden or not, never a base (index 1) definition; in an object without `versym` every definition matches every request (the lookup stays permissive: a program that needs a version from an object without version tables is REFUSED like the reference loader, exit 127 and a message naming the object and the version, with no warn-and-continue and no COMPAT option; that refusal belongs to the load-time version check, DL-10 in the plan, not to the lookup; coordinator ruling #3655). Names are compared as bytes, no node is special (`LIELLA_PRIVATE` included, R14-12). **Scopes** (design §5): global; global then the dlopen group (local first with `RTLD_DEEPBIND`); `RTLD_NEXT` = after the caller in the global scope, else in its local scope; a COPY lookup excludes the program. **Binding:** the first object in scope order that defines the name wins, weak or strong (probe: link order decides, `LD_DYNAMIC_WEAK=1` changes nothing); an undefined weak reference binds 0, an undefined strong one is `Undefined`; an `STB_GNU_UNIQUE` definition is replaced by the namespace registry's entry for (name, version name), or recorded there (probe: shared across two `RTLD_LOCAL` dlopens). Version names are found by walking `DT_VERDEF` per lookup (a per-object index is the L14-7 memo, later). (Amended by D-27.27, D-27.42.) |

| D-27.15 | §27 | SEC | **The general object mapper (phase 14 DL-7, DL-MAP; design §3, L14-5; threat model "The dynamic loader" rule 4).** `liella_ld::map` (pure; the system calls through the `Mapper` trait, implemented by `SysMapper` in `boundary/src/ld.rs`). `plan` validates before anything is mapped: `ET_DYN` or `ET_EXEC` (`NotLoadable`); any number of `PT_LOAD`s (no count bound: DL-MAP-PROBE probed the reference loader on 2026-11-10 with objects of 64, 65, 100 to 1100, 4000, 10000 and 30000 `PT_LOAD`s, and it loaded every one through both `ld.so PROGRAM` and `dlopen`; the work stays linear in `e_phnum`, which the ELF reader bounds; the 64 bound of DL-MAP is removed, no differences row); each `PT_LOAD` non-empty (`p_memsz` > 0), `p_filesz` ≤ `p_memsz`, `p_offset` ≡ `p_vaddr` modulo the page, `p_align` 0, 1 or a power of two ≤ 2^46, file bytes inside the file (reader), never `PF_W` with `PF_X` (`WriteExec`); segments in address order and never sharing a page; span ≤ 2^46; an `ET_EXEC` ends at or below `Arch::USER_END`; a `PT_GNU_RELRO` range inside the span (whole pages recorded, `BadSegments` otherwise). `load`: one `PROT_NONE` reservation; `ET_DYN` anywhere, over-reserved by `align - page` and trimmed so the bias is a multiple of the largest `p_align` (also when the first segment is not at 0); `ET_EXEC` at its link-time address with `MAP_FIXED_NOREPLACE` (`Placement` when taken, or when the kernel places it elsewhere). Each segment `MAP_FIXED` inside the reservation with exactly its `p_flags` protection; the `.bss` bytes sharing the last file page are zeroed (writable segment), or, for a read-only segment with `.bss` (no linker emits it, handled for correctness), that page is mapped as zero pages read-write, the file bytes copied, then set to the segment's protection (never W+X at any moment); the rest of the `.bss` anonymous pages. Gaps between segments stay reserved `PROT_NONE` (guard). Any failed call unmaps the whole reservation (`System`). The RELRO range is kept in `Loaded`; `Loaded::protect_relro` applies it after relocation (DL-10). Page size: `Arch::page_size(&Auxv)` = `AT_PAGESZ` when a power of two ≥ `Arch::BASE_PAGE`, else `BASE_PAGE` (x86_64 4096, the only page literal); `ld.rs` passes it to the mapper and the RELRO protection. A program without `PT_DYNAMIC` has no relocations or dependencies: ld.so enters it after RELRO. Messages: `ld.so: <path>: <reason>`, status 127. Proof: `crates/ld/tests/map.rs` (model address space; corpus; `/proc/self/maps` via the product); fuzz target `ld_map`. \| DL-7 row; design §3 |
| D-27.16 | §27 | SEC | **Library search, the cache reader and `--list` (phase 14 DL-8, DL-SEARCH-CACHE; design §4 and §19; R14-3 (a), R14-15, R14-18, owner #940 and #941; clause s27_1_c_1_1).** `liella_ld::search` (pure, no allocation; the boundary opens): a name with `/` is tried as given after token expansion; Liella's pinned sonames (`search::PINNED`: libc, libm, the DL-1 placeholders, `libc_malloc_debug.so.0`) resolve to `<prefix>/lib` only, after `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` outside secure mode (R14-3: the override is for testing a libc build), never through RPATH, RUNPATH, the cache or another directory; the loader's own name is the loaded loader. Otherwise: `DT_RPATH` of the requester and of each object that loaded it up to the program (an object's RPATH only when it has no RUNPATH; all of them only when the requester has none), `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` (`:` or `;`; ignored in secure mode), the requester's `DT_RUNPATH`, the cache, the default directories. Each directory is tried with the supported `glibc-hwcaps` subdirectories first, highest first (`Arch::hwcaps`, the x86-64 psABI levels from the same `Features` libc dispatches on). Tokens `$ORIGIN`, `$LIB`, `$PLATFORM` (bare or braced); an unknown token skips the element. Secure mode (threat model rules 1-3): `$ORIGIN` only when the object's directory is trusted, `LD_ORIGIN_PATH` ignored, an element empty or relative after expansion skipped; outside it an empty element is `.`. Prefix: compile-time `LIELLA_PREFIX`, default `/`; cache `<prefix>/etc/ld.so.cache`; default directories `Arch::SYSTEM_DIRS` when the prefix is `/` (the reference's `ld.so --help` list: `/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu`, `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu`, `/lib`, `/usr/lib`), else `<prefix>/lib`; trusted (threat model rule 5 as amended by owner #4237): `<prefix>/lib` for another prefix, and for `/` exactly `Arch::SYSTEM_DIRS` (`/lib64` and `/usr/lib64` are not trusted). `$LIB` = `lib/x86_64-linux-gnu` (DL-0b probe); `$PLATFORM` = `haswell` for an x86-64-v3 or v4 CPU (probed on Haswell only), `x86_64` otherwise. `liella_ld::cache`: new format only (#941; old and compat files are "no cache"); every offset, count and string end checked against the file and the string table, an entry whose path does not start with `/` is inconsistent (a relative path would be opened from the current directory), any inconsistency on the way of a lookup = not in the cache. Lookup: binary search under the Appendix D.3.3 comparison (digit runs numeric, so `1.09` matches `1.9` as the reference's does), then the run of equal keys in file order: entries whose flags are not `Arch::CACHE_FLAGS` skipped, a legacy hwcap word skipped, the best supported hwcaps entry before the first plain entry, else that plain entry (#940). `ld.so --list PROGRAM`, `LD_TRACE_LOADED_OBJECTS` (kernel start or `ld.so PROGRAM`; ignored in secure mode, rule 11): every needed object found and mapped through `map::load` breadth first, each once (name or `DT_SONAME`), a file that is not this architecture's object skipped and the search continued; lines `\tlinux-vdso.so.1 (0x…)`, `\tNAME => PATH (0xBIAS)`, `\tNAME => not found`, then the program's `PT_INTERP` with the loader's base; the lines are written after the walk; a dependency not found is `\tNAME => not found` with status 0 when tracing, and with `--list` the loader's error (`PROG: error while loading shared libraries: NAME: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory`) on stderr, nothing on stdout, status 127 (both probed on the reference, DL-SEARCH-CACHE-2). Bounds: 256 objects and 64 KiB of paths per list (refused beyond, with a message); paths over `PATH_MAX` skipped. Running a program with dependencies stays refused until DL-10 relocates them. |
| D-27.17 | §27 | SEC | **Eager relocation of loaded objects (phase 14 DL-10, DL-RELOC and DL-RELOC-2; design §6; R14-13, D-27.11; amends D-27.15 for empty segments).** `liella_ld::reloc` (pure; memory through the `Image` trait, `ProcImage` in `boundary/src/ld.rs`). Arithmetic only through `Arch::apply` (x86-64 psABI §4.4.1: RELATIVE/IRELATIVE B+A, 64 S+A, GLOB_DAT and JUMP_SLOT S, the 32/32S/PC32 text widths checked for fit). Order: objects in reverse load order (dependencies before their users, the program last); per object RELR, RELA, JMPREL; IRELATIVE and references bound to an IFUNC are deferred to a second pass after every plain store of that object, so a resolver never runs before the data it may read is relocated. COPY: only in the program, looked up in the global scope without the program, copies min(program size, definition size). TEXTREL: the read-only segments are made read-write (never executable and writable at once) for pass 1 and restored before any resolver runs; a deferred store into text is refused. Every store is checked to lie inside a writable `PT_LOAD` (or a text segment opened for TEXTREL). TLS relocation kinds are refused (DL-12). RELRO is protected after relocation. Version check before relocation (D-27.11): a versioned need from an object without version definitions stops with status 127 naming the object and version; a missing version stops with status 1; weak needs are skipped. Dependencies load by path only until DL-8; one object reached by two paths (symlink, hard link) is loaded once, identity (`st_dev`, `st_ino`) of the opened file (L14-4, ruling #4231). A program asking for an executable stack (`PT_GNU_STACK` with `PF_X`) and any such dependency are refused (R14-13). An empty `PT_LOAD` (`p_memsz` 0; binutils 2.42 emits one for `-z notext`; the gABI allows it) is skipped and never mapped, amending D-27.15's "each `PT_LOAD` non-empty". When the dynamic symbol count is only a lower bound (no SysV hash and a GNU hash table whose buckets are all empty, as a program exporting nothing has), the symbol table's index limit is raised to cover every RELA/JMPREL symbol; objects that hash a symbol pay nothing. Open: a program started through `PT_INTERP` is still read from `/proc/self/exe`; ruling #4229 replaces that with a reader over the memory image (`AT_PHDR`), DL-RELOC-3. Proof: `crates/ld/tests/reloc.rs` (arithmetic, model corpus, version check, ld.so runs: multi-object both modes, unversioned stub, executable stack, RELRO, two paths); plants handoff/DL-RELOC-2-plants.txt. (Amended by D-27.18.) |
| D-27.18 | §27 | SEC | **The program is read from its memory image, never from its file (ruling #4229, coordinator ruling #4323; amends D-27.17).** `link` (`boundary/src/ld.rs`) no longer opens `/proc/self/exe` (nor the program's path for `ld.so PROGRAM`): it fails without `/proc` and can read a file other than the one executed. The reader has an image mode, `Elf::from_image(phdrs, spans)`: `spans` map link-time ranges to bytes, and every address must lie in the file-backed part of one `PT_LOAD` and wholly in one span, as for a file. Aliasing rule (a shared slice alive across the relocator's raw stores would be undefined behaviour): `Elf::image_span_kind` slices a `PT_LOAD` in place (`Live`) only when its bytes cannot change during loading: readable, not `PF_W`, the object not text-relocated, and overlapping no segment the relocator may store into (the relocator stores only into `PF_W` segments of such an object: `inside()` stays). Anything read from a range that can change is COPIED (not read through raw-pointer reads) into anonymous mappings before the first relocation store: the program header table and `PT_DYNAMIC` always (one small mapping each), and the whole file-backed part of a changing `PT_LOAD` that holds a table named by `DT_STRTAB`, `DT_SYMTAB`, `DT_HASH`, `DT_GNU_HASH`, `DT_VERSYM`, `DT_VERDEF`, `DT_VERNEED`, `DT_RELA`, `DT_JMPREL` or `DT_RELR` (in practice only a text-relocated program, whose read-only segments are made writable for relocation). Why copies: the reader keeps its slice API (raw reads would touch every table walker and the file path too), a copy cannot alias by construction, and the cost falls only on the rare layouts (one copy of `PT_DYNAMIC` otherwise). Text-relocated programs are run, not refused (#4323): RW for relocation, RX again before any code of theirs runs (L14-6). The image header is synthesized (`ET_DYN`, the table's `e_phnum`); the file-offset overlap checks do not apply. Any number of `PT_LOAD`s, as for a library (no count bound, D-27.15): the span list is sized from the table (`e_phnum` spans: one per `PT_LOAD` and one for the `PT_DYNAMIC` copy, after the copied table in its mapping, so no extra system call). The program has no (dev, ino) identity any more: a dependency naming the program's own file is loaded as a separate object (ruling #4341: accepted until a case needs it). **Load bias (ruling #4371):** `PT_PHDR`'s `p_vaddr` subtracted from `AT_PHDR` when the program has one; without it (`liella_ld::start::bias`), the ELF header at the start of the page holding `AT_PHDR` (checked: magic, `e_phoff` equal to the table's offset in that page, `e_phentsize`, `e_phnum`) gives `e_phoff`, and the `PT_LOAD` whose file-backed part holds the table gives its link-time address `p_vaddr - p_offset + e_phoff`; a program whose header does not check out there is refused, never run at bias 0. The program's RELRO pages use that same bias (`rt::start::relro_at`), for `ld.so PROGRAM` too. Tests: `reloc_image_reader_slices_only_unchanging_segments`, `reloc_ldso_kernel_started_without_proc` (root without `/proc` through `unshare -r --root`), `reloc_ldso_program_without_pt_phdr`, `reloc_ldso_textrel_program_text_rx_before_it_runs`, `map_proc_self_maps_of_loaded_programs` (300 `PT_LOAD`s run as `ld.so PROGRAM`); plants handoff/DL-IMAGE-READER-plants.txt. Miri was not run (the access pattern crosses the process image and raw syscalls); the targeted test checks the invariant Miri would. |
| D-27.19 | §1.1, §27 | — | **Constructor and destructor order in ld.so (phase 14 DL-11, DL-INIT-ORDER; design §9).** `liella_ld::init` (pure) and `run_init`/`fini_all` in `boundary/src/ld.rs`. After relocation and RELRO of the whole start set: the program's `DT_PREINIT_ARRAY` (a shared object's is ignored), then each shared object's `DT_INIT` then `DT_INIT_ARRAY` in order, each called with `(argc, argv, envp)`. The program's own `DT_INIT`/`DT_INIT_ARRAY` are left to its C library's start (the reference loader runs neither for a program without one). Order: objects indexed in load order, object 0 the root (the program; the object named to `dlopen` later); a depth-first walk over objects 1..n in reverse load order, each placed after the objects it names in `DT_NEEDED` (in their order); a dependency already being walked (a cycle) is passed over; the root is never entered from another object and comes last. Fini: the same walk over every object loaded at the time, reversed (program first): `DT_FINI_ARRAY` in reverse then `DT_FINI`, through the termination function the loader passes in `%rdx` (`liella_machine_ld_enter` no longer zeroes it), run once. Array entries 0 and all-ones are not called (no spec clause; calling them could only fault). Probe-settled, black box: tools/probe/dl/order.sh (diamond, ties, a dependency reached through a later sibling, two- and three-object cycles, a retagged preinit array in a shared object; exit order from the same programs linked with the C library) and DL-0b's `== order` record (the `dlopen` cycle H <-> I initialises I then H: the root-last rule). Open: the `dlopen`/`dlclose` path and `__cxa_finalize` per object come with the dlopen story; a dynamic program without `DT_NEEDED` still enters with `%rdx` = 0 and runs no preinit array. Proof: `crates/ld/tests/init_order.rs` (pure orders; the corpus under the built ld.so equal line for line to the reference's record, and live against the reference); plants handoff/DL-INIT-ORDER-plants.txt. |
| D-27.20 | §22.6, §27.3 | — | **Static TLS of the initially loaded objects (DL-12 `DL-TLS-STATIC`, design §7, R14-4).** `liella_ld::tls` lays out the static TLS of the program and its dependencies as pure logic over the `Arch` table (new rows: `TLS_VARIANT`, `TCB_SIZE`, `TCB_ALIGN`, `SELF_SLOT`, `DTV_SLOT`, `STACK_GUARD_SLOT`, `POINTER_GUARD_SLOT`, `DTP_BIAS`, `TP_BIAS`, `apply_tls`). Offsets follow Drepper, "ELF Handling For Thread-Local Storage" §3.4 (variant II for x86_64: the program's block ends at TP, later modules below it in load order; variant I implemented from the same paper, tested by A-4), extended so that a block keeps `p_vaddr mod p_align`. Module IDs start at 1 over the objects with `PT_TLS`, in load order. Below the last block: a 64 KiB surplus of untouched anonymous memory (R14-4). **The initial area** is one anonymous mapping: surplus, blocks, Liella's thread block at TP (FLAG_OWN, self words, canary and pointer guard taken from AT_RANDOM through the provisional block, `%fs:0x28`/`%fs:0x30`), then the dtv. Images are copied after relocation (a `.tdata` word may hold a relocated address) and only from inside a `PT_LOAD`'s file part (else the object is refused). **The dtv** is Liella's own layout: word 0 the generation it was built for, word 1 the slot count, word 1+m module m's block. **Relocations:** `DTPMOD64` (no symbol: the object's own module), `DTPOFF64` and `TPOFF64` via `Arch::apply_tls`; an `STT_TLS` symbol's value is not moved by the load bias; a TLS relocation against an object without `PT_TLS` is refused; `TLSDESC` stays refused (later story, R14-8 primitives). **`__tls_get_addr`** is exported by `ld.so` at the version `spec/abi/versions.tsv` gives it (`GLIBC_2.3`; `cargo xtask so` writes the version script from the table); it refuses a thread block without FLAG_OWN (D-5.11 safety: never read another loader's block word as a pointer), then compares the generation and the slot count before reading a slot; anything else is a failure until the dlopen family adds the slow path. An object naming the interpreter's soname (`DT_NEEDED`) gets the running interpreter (its file read for the tables, its image not relocated again), so `__tls_get_addr` resolves in the global scope. Tests: `crates/ld/tests/tls.rs` (layout, arithmetic, dtv lookup; the LE/IE/GD/LD matrix over a program and two libraries, alignments 4-64, as `ld.so PROG` and through `PT_INTERP`). Not covered: variant I host tests (A-4), TLSDESC, threads (DL-13 `__liella_tls_init`). (Amended by D-27.23, D-27.36, D-27.39.) |
| D-27.21 | §27 | SEC | **libc finds the executable's load bias as `ld.so` does, from one implementation (escalations #4371, #4414, #4422, #4476; design point #4528; amends D-27.12).** Without the static-PIE start's bias, libc's one source of the executable's bias (`exe_bias` in `boundary/src/process.rs`: `dl_iterate_phdr`, `_dl_find_object`, the `%n` check, the backtrace) used `PT_PHDR` only, so a dynamically linked program without `PT_PHDR` was seen at bias 0. It now uses `liella_rt::start::bias` (D-27.18's method: `PT_PHDR`, or without one the ELF header at the start of the page holding `AT_PHDR` and the `PT_LOAD` holding the program headers; 0 when neither gives one). The function lives where libc's start lives (`liella_rt::start`) and `liella_ld::start` re-exports it, so `ld.so` and libc cannot disagree. It reads no header when there are no program headers. Start-up does not call it: the static start keeps `start::program`'s one pass (a static ET_EXEC's bias is 0, a static PIE's comes from its relocator). Test: `reloc_libc_bias_without_pt_phdr` (crates/ld/tests/reloc.rs), a PIE and an ET_EXEC linked against `libc.so.6` with `PT_PHDR` removed, kernel-started and as `ld.so PROGRAM`, and a static ET_EXEC. |
| D-27.22 | §27 | SEC | **`LIELLA_PRIVATE` start interface: a build tag checked at load, and `__liella_libc_early_init` before any constructor (phase 14 DL-13, plan/ph14/design.md §14, L14-10, R14-12).** `libc.so.6` exports two symbols at its own version node `LIELLA_PRIVATE` (never in a public header): `__liella_build_tag`, 64 bytes (`LIELLA-BUILD-TAG:` then the build's identity, zero-filled), and `__liella_libc_early_init(const StartInfo *)` (`liella_rt::start::private`, shared by both products so the C library's code does not depend on the loader crate; the lookup and check are `liella_ld::start::private::find`: argc, argv, envp, auxv, stack end, `repr(C)`). The identity is FNV-1a 64 over the product sources (`crates/`, `csys/`, `include/`, `Cargo.lock`; paths sorted, so no file-system order enters it), computed by `cargo xtask so` and passed as `LIELLA_BUILD_TAG` to both product builds; a source hash rather than the commit because the build roles are synced copies without git, and it also separates two dirty trees at one commit. After the version check and before any relocation, `ld.so` looks up `__liella_libc_early_init@LIELLA_PRIVATE` in each loaded object but itself; the first object defining it must define `__liella_build_tag@LIELLA_PRIVATE` as a 64-byte object inside the file part of a `PT_LOAD`, equal to `ld.so`'s own tag, else the start stops with `<object>: LIELLA_PRIVATE build tag differs from the dynamic loader's ...` and status 127 (no code of the library has run). After relocation, RELRO and the static TLS images, `ld.so` calls the entry with the initial stack before the program's `.preinit_array`; it publishes the auxiliary vector, `environ`, the program names and `__libc_stack_end` and runs the tunables and the CPU-path selection (start steps 3 and 4, step 3 through the inlined helper `__libc_start_main` uses; its tunables parse prints no diagnostics, as `ld.so` read the string; `__libc_start_main`'s own step 4 is unchanged, so the static path keeps its code and hot-text keys). The NULL-folding guard needs no early step: it is decided at the first small copy or fill. Until DL-14, `__libc_start_main` repeats steps 3 and 4 with the same values. The export moves (`__libc_stack_end`, the `__rseq_*` objects to `ld.so`) and rseq publishing by `ld.so` are not part of this record (DL-13's second half). Tests: a `.preinit_array` function sees `getenv` work and `memcpy(NULL, NULL, 0)`/`memset(NULL, 0, 0)` return, kernel-started and as `ld.so PROGRAM`; a copy of `libc.so.6` with one tag byte changed is refused with the diagnostic. |
| D-27.23 | §27.3 | SEC | **The interpreter's own scope entry comes from its mapped image (DL-TLS-SELF-IMAGE; ruling #4501, family of #4229).** When an initially loaded object names the interpreter's soname (`DT_NEEDED`, for `__tls_get_addr`), `ld.so` enters itself in the scope from its memory image through the image-mode reader of D-27.18: its ELF header at its own run-time base (the first bytes of its first `PT_LOAD`) gives the program header table, and `image_view` builds the spans as for the program. It opens no file of its own at start-up: neither the program's `PT_INTERP` path nor `/proc/self/exe` (D-27.20 read one of them). Gains: one open, one mapping and one close fewer at start-up; start-up works without `/proc` and when the interpreter's file may be executed but not read; no path that could be replaced between the kernel's mapping and a second open is trusted. The interpreter keeps its D-27.20 treatment otherwise: never relocated again, its initialisers not run by the loader's initialiser pass. Its `(dev, ino)` is not known (no file is read), so a dependency naming the interpreter's file by path rather than by soname is loaded separately (the case ruling #4341 accepted for the program). Tests: `tls_interpreter_scope_entry_without_reading_its_file` (execute-only interpreter, `PT_INTERP` and `ld.so PROGRAM`), `tls_model_matrix_over_initially_loaded_objects`; plants handoff/DL-TLS-SELF-IMAGE-plants.txt. |
| D-27.24 | §1.1, §27 | SEC | **`__libc_start_main` under Liella's `ld.so` (phase 14 DL-14, plan/ph14/design.md §14): start steps 1-4 run once, in libc's early init; libc runs the program's `DT_INIT`/`DT_INIT_ARRAY`.** Detection: `__liella_libc_early_init` (D-27.22) sets a libc-private flag as its last act, and `__libc_start_main` takes the dynamic path when the thread pointer is set and the flag is set; only Liella's `ld.so` calls the early init, so no other loader's thread block is read to decide, and a static program tests the flag only after its own `ARCH_GET_FS` answer (its start does no added work). The dynamic path skips steps 1-4 (thread block, secure-mode clearing, tunables and CPU paths); it keeps `set_tid_address`, threads forbidden until DL-15 gives them the loader's TLS interface, the program's `__fpu_control` (D-10.5, #814), the heap perturb byte, the name-service cache, the initial descriptor and the internal signal, registers `rtld_fini` (every object's `DT_FINI_ARRAY`/`DT_FINI`, the program's included), then publishes the initial `environ` and program names again before the program's own initialisation: a `.preinit_array` function's `setenv`, `unsetenv` or change of `program_invocation_name` is undone, a constructor's reaches `main` (the reference's output for the same program, black-box probe 2026-11-11; a static program keeps both, as its start runs `.preinit_array` itself). The `fini` an old-style start object passes is not registered: `rtld_fini` already runs the program's `.fini_array`, so calling `fini` too would run it twice for a pre-2.34 `__libc_csu_fini` (the reference never calls it either, same probe). The loader runs the program's `.preinit_array` and every shared object's initialisation and passes the program's `DT_INIT` and `DT_INIT_ARRAY` in `StartInfo` (same build, tag-checked); libc runs them after all shared objects when `init` is NULL (2.34+ start objects) or calls `init` (pre-2.34 start objects), each with `(argc, argv, envp)`, harmless to a `void (*)(void)` under the psABI and what an `init` that runs the arrays itself passes on. Secure mode: the early init opens `/dev/null` on a closed descriptor 0, 1 or 2 before any constructor runs (s1_1_g_3), so a constructor of a privileged program never gets a standard descriptor number from `open`. Proof: `reloc_libc_start_hello_world` (output equal to a stated text, the reference's output for the same source by probe, so the test does not depend on the host's library; three start objects; kernel-started and `ld.so PROGRAM`) and `sym___fpu_control` (the dynamic `fpu_control_*` conformance programs run on Liella; the #814 skip is lifted). Plants: handoff/DL-LIBC-START-plants.txt. |
| D-27.25 | §1.1, §27 | SEC | **The self-relocator accepts any number of writable `PT_LOAD`s** (DL-MULTI-WRITABLE, owner ruling #4655: "All the security in the world is useless if it doesn't work."). Amends D-27.10 rule (2), which required exactly one: a static PIE whose data is aligned above 4 KiB (a 16 KiB-aligned `.data1` makes GNU ld 2.42 start a new writable segment) and a program run by `ld.so` with two writable segments were refused at start (exit 127). The ELF format allows any number of `PT_LOAD`s with any flags. Now `liella_ld::boot::image` needs one `PT_DYNAMIC` and at least one writable `PT_LOAD`, keeps the program headers and lists the writable segments from them (no copy, no allocation: the relocator runs before the heap and before relocation). Each relocation target is located in the writable segment that holds all 8 of its bytes (`boot::Writer`; the segment of the last target is tried first, so a run of targets in one segment costs one range check each) and written through that segment's own view (`boot::Memory`, made by `boundary/src/bootstrap.rs` for one store, category *slice*). **Checks that stay** (D-27.10, `ann = SEC`): a target outside every writable segment, or straddling two, is refused (`BootError::Outside`, exit 127 before any relocated data is read); a writable segment whose end overflows the address space is refused; every relocation table holds whole entries and overlaps no writable segment (the relocator never reads what it writes); `DT_TEXTREL`, a wrong `DT_RELAENT`/`DT_RELRENT`/`DT_PLTREL`, a missing `DT_NULL`, a RELR bitmap before an address and address overflow are refused; only `Relative` in pass 1 and `Irelative` in pass 2; no panics; no write outside a mapped segment (a view is made only for a segment the headers name writable); the mapper's refusal of a writable-and-executable segment and the secure-mode rules are unchanged. The unit tests' memory gives each segment a view that runs past its end, so only the relocator's own check can refuse a target in a gap. `ld.so`'s general relocator (`liella_ld::reloc`) and the image reader already accepted any number of writable segments. **RELRO across segments:** a `PT_GNU_RELRO` may span several writable `PT_LOAD`s (GNU ld 2.42 keeps it inside one; the ELF format does not). Its pages are made read-only segment by segment: the part inside each `PT_LOAD`'s pages (`liella_rt::start::relro_pieces`/`relro_piece`), so a page between two segments (unmapped, or `ld.so`'s reservation) is never changed. `ld.so` does this for its objects (`reloc::protect_relro`) and for a program it relocates with the self-relocator; a static program keeps its one `mprotect` of the whole range (the start-up path does no added work) and walks the headers again only if that call fails, which an unmapped page between kernel-mapped segments causes. One segment gives the one range as before. |
| D-27.26 | §27 | ABI | **`__libc_stack_end` and the rseq objects are `ld.so`'s; `ld.so` registers the initial thread's rseq area (phase 14 DL-13, plan/ph14/design.md §14, R14-12).** Liella's `ld.so` exports `__libc_stack_end@@GLIBC_2.2.5`, `__rseq_offset@@GLIBC_2.35`, `__rseq_size@@GLIBC_2.35` and `__rseq_flags@@GLIBC_2.35`, as spec/abi/versions.tsv places them; `libc.so.6` keeps its own copies local (they serve `libc.a`'s static programs, unchanged) and never refers to the loader's, so no libc-side code names the loader crate (D-27.22's dependency rule). For a dynamically linked program `ld.so` reserves, above the initial thread's pointer, the thread block and room up to `liella_rt::tls::RSEQ_OFFSET + 32` (where the C library's descriptor holds the rseq area in every other thread, so `__rseq_offset` is one value for all threads), maps that area before relocating any object, registers the 32-byte rseq area there (unless `glibc.pthread.rseq=0`), and publishes `__rseq_offset`/`__rseq_size` and `__libc_stack_end` (the initial stack pointer) before relocation, so a program's copy relocation of one reads its final value. The registered size travels to the C library in `StartInfo.rseq_size` (`__liella_libc_early_init`); when it is non-zero, the threads `libc.so.6` creates register their own areas at the same offset. Static programs and the program-alone start (no `DT_NEEDED`) are unchanged. |
| D-27.27 | §27.1 | — | **A relocation's versioned reference accepts a base definition (amends D-27.11; DL-LIBC-START-6).** `liella_ld::symbols::Want::Reference(version)` is what `Object::reference_want` now gives for a reference whose `versym` index names a version: the definition of exactly that version (hidden or not), else a base (index 1) definition, so an unversioned definition earlier in the scope interposes on a versioned reference; an exact definition later in the same object's chain still wins over a base one. `Want::Version` (`dlvsym`, the start-up handshake) keeps D-27.11's rule that a base definition never matches a name. Probe-settled (spec/behaviour/dynlink.md "Symbol binding", black box against glibc 2.39): `libv.so`'s own `f@@VER_1` `JUMP_SLOT` binds to an unversioned `f` in the program and in an `LD_PRELOAD` object, both with `versym`, and a program's needed `f@VER_1` (`vna_other`) binds to the preloaded `f` too. This is how a program's `__fpu_control` reaches `libc.so.6`'s `GLOB_DAT` reference (D-10.5): before it, Liella's ld.so bound libc's reference to libc's own definition and a dynamic program's x87 control word stayed 0x037f. Proof: the `Reference` rows of `versions_bind_like_the_reference`, `sym___fpu_control` (dynamic, under Liella's ld.so); plants handoff/DL-LIBC-START-6-plants.txt. |
| D-27.28 | §1.2, §27 | — | **Liella ships its own link-time archive `libc_nonshared.a` and an installed `libc.so` linker script (owner ruling #4807).** A program or shared object links against an installed Liella with no host C library file. `cargo xtask so` builds both into the product directory. The script is `GROUP ( libc.so.6 libc_nonshared.a AS_NEEDED ( ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 ) )`, with bare names found on the library search path where the products are installed, never an absolute host path. The members are `atexit`, `at_quick_exit`, `__pthread_atfork` with `pthread_atfork` as a weak alias, and `__stack_chk_fail_local`. They come from `csys/nonshared/` and the list is settled by black-box probes in spec/behaviour/dynlink.md ("The link-time archive"). Each member is a one-statement function linked into the CALLER's module, hidden, with no state of its own. It passes the value of that module's `__dso_handle` to the libc.so.6 function that owns the list: `__cxa_atexit@GLIBC_2.2.5`, `__cxa_at_quick_exit@GLIBC_2.10` or `__register_atfork@GLIBC_2.3.2`. `__stack_chk_fail_local` calls `__stack_chk_fail@GLIBC_2.4`. Because of that tag, `__cxa_finalize` at unload runs or drops the module's registrations. The build checks that each member defines exactly its names and that all of them are hidden. **Two-way compatibility (the reason for the archive form).** Code built against Liella needs only `GLIBC_*` versions, so it also runs on the reference. The test links with `-L <products> -lc`, reads the link maps (Liella's archive is loaded; no host `libc.so.6`, `libc.so`, `libc_nonshared.a` or `libc.a`) and checks `readelf -V`. It then runs the program and a `dlopen`ed shared object on the reference. The dynamic conformance subset links with Liella's archive in place of the host's. **Shipped and supported now; deprecation intended later (owner intent, 2026-11-11).** The archive is supported today as the way unversioned `atexit`, `at_quick_exit` and `pthread_atfork` references bind. The owner intends to deprecate it eventually, so that distributions adopting Liella can migrate away from it over time. No deprecation action (no warning, no notice, no behaviour change) is taken until a viable replacement exists. DL-NONSHARED-OPTOUT explores one: a version-node opt-in with loader-side module attribution (handoff/DL-NONSHARED-OPTOUT.md). **Open (not this record):** Liella's `__cxa_finalize(dso)` runs the module's exit handlers and forgets its quick-exit handlers, but it does not yet drop the module's atfork handlers, which the reference's does (probe in spec/behaviour/dynlink.md). Liella's loader has no `dlclose` yet (phase 14), so this is not reachable today. The atfork list needs a module slot first. |
| D-27.30 | §27 | — | **`dlopen`: one object chain, one writer lock, one publication point before the constructors (phase 14 DL-16, plan/ph14/dl-16-dlopen.md §1 and §4; refines plan/ph14/design.md §5 and §9).** One namespace, `LM_ID_BASE`; the loaded objects form one append-only chain owned by `ld.so`. One writer lock per namespace: a futex lock inside `ld.so` (no libc calls), re-entrant for its owning thread; `dlopen` (later `dlclose` and `dlmopen`) holds it for the whole call. Readers take no lock (D-27.1): `dl_iterate_phdr`, `_dl_find_object`, `dladdr`, `dlsym`, the lazy resolver and the slow path of `__tls_get_addr` read published state only, each through one function, `read_section`, which is empty in DL-16 and gets DL-17's per-thread reader epochs. Publication is one point per `dlopen`, after the second relocation pass and before the constructors: the chain append, the global-scope append, the address index and `dlpi_adds` together, so code that a constructor starts in another thread can unwind through and look up the new objects; `dlopen` returns after the constructors. Why: lock-free readers keep unwinding and `dl_iterate_phdr` off the writer's path (callbacks run without the lock, ruling #2607), a constructor that waits on a thread calling `dlsym` cannot deadlock, and DL-17 adds reclamation without changing any reader. |
| D-27.31 | §27 | SEC | **A failed `dlopen` leaves no trace (phase 14 DL-16, plan/ph14/dl-16-dlopen.md §2 and §3; DLOPEN-FAILURE-PATHS folded in, #2629).** Relocation of a new set runs in two passes. Pass 1 resolves every symbol reference of the whole set (memo by symbol index, L14-7), checks versions (`VERNEED` against `VERDEF`) and places TLS; it may fail and runs no foreign code. Pass 2 applies the relocations in D-27.17's order and cannot fail. So every failure point comes before the first IFUNC resolver or constructor of the attempt. The way back, in reverse order: TLS module ids and surplus ranges released; every new object's reservation unmapped (D-27.15) and its descriptor closed; counts bumped on already-loaded objects restored; nothing published (chain, scopes, unique table, address index); the attempt's loader-arena memory freed; one dlerror text set. `dlpi_adds` and `dlpi_subs` follow the probe: a refusal at the header changes neither, an attempt that mapped k objects bumps both by k (they count objects ever mapped and ever unmapped). Why: a half-loaded object, or a resolver that ran for an object that never loads, is state no caller can see or undo. Plants: skip the root's unmap on a missing dependency; skip restoring a dependency's count; publish before pass 1 ends. Probe P-10 records whether the reference runs IFUNC resolvers in a failing `dlopen`; if it does, a neutral differences row. |
| D-27.32 | §27 | SEC | **`dlopen` handles and counts (phase 14 DL-16 and DL-17, plan/ph14/dl-16-dlopen.md §1 and §2; coordinator ruling #5006).** A handle is the address of Liella's per-object record (equal to its `struct link_map`, probe P-12). `dlsym` and `dlvsym` (and `dlclose` in DL-17) refuse a handle that Liella did not return, or one already closed, with a dlerror text and no other effect: the secure default. The check stays cheap: `RTLD_DEFAULT`, `RTLD_NEXT` and the NULL handle are recognised first, then one lookup in the existing address index or a handle set kept with the chain; never a scan of the chain on the `dlsym` path. `opens` counts direct `dlopen` calls (a re-open, `RTLD_NOLOAD` included, adds one); DL-16 never decrements it; it saturates at `u32::MAX` and the object becomes `nodelete`, because a wrapped count could unmap a live object in DL-17. One differences row, shared with DL-17's `dlclose`. No compatibility option: the documented interface leaves any other handle undefined, and restoring a crash has no value. |
| D-27.33 | §27 | ABI | **`dlopen` in statically linked programs is deferred to a later phase-14 item (coordinator ruling #5005; plan/ph14/dl-16-dlopen.md §7).** DL-16 builds `dlopen` for dynamically linked programs (Liella's `ld.so`). In a program linked with `libc.a`, `dlopen` returns NULL and sets a dlerror text, and `dlsym` and `dlvsym` fail the same way: never a crash, and never an undefined symbol at link time (`libc.a` carries the failing entry points from DL-16a). Loading objects into a static program is its own phase-14 story, DL-16S `DL-DLOPEN-STATIC`, after DL-17 and DL-20: it needs unloading and lazy binding to be useful. Until then a differences row records the difference and a compatibility option id is registered for it (records/pending/DL-16-PLAN-5.toml, status registered, not implemented). Deferred, not dropped. |
| D-27.34 | §27 | — | **What the DL-16P probes settle for DL-16 (`dlopen`/`dlsym`, plan/ph14/dl-16-dlopen.md §1-4).** Each item follows the reference as probed (`spec/behaviour/dynlink.md`, section "dlopen and dlsym probes P-1..P-13"; probes `tools/probe/dl/dlopen/`). (1) **Mode bits (P-1):** a mode with any bit outside `RTLD_LAZY\|RTLD_NOW\|RTLD_NOLOAD\|RTLD_DEEPBIND\|RTLD_GLOBAL\|RTLD_NODELETE` fails before the search with the dlerror text `invalid mode parameter` (also without a binding mode); `RTLD_NOW\|RTLD_LAZY` binds lazily (eagerly until DL-20, the phase's interim gap). (2) **Identity (P-2):** a bare name (no `/`) is first compared with the `DT_SONAME` of every loaded object (for `dlopen` and `DT_NEEDED` alike), never with file names; a found file is then compared by `(st_dev, st_ino)`; `l_name` keeps the name of the first open. (3) **`RTLD_GLOBAL` (P-3):** a first open or a promotion (`NOLOAD\|GLOBAL`, or a plain re-open with `GLOBAL`) appends the opened object's whole local scope (itself, then its dependencies breadth-first, those not yet global) to the global scope. (4) **Lookup scopes (P-5):** `RTLD_NEXT` searches the objects after the caller in the scope the caller was loaded with (the global scope for start-time objects, the root's local scope for a `dlopen`'d object); `RTLD_DEFAULT` from a `dlopen`'d object searches the global scope, then the caller's local scope; failure texts name the calling object. (5) **dlerror (P-6):** every `dl*` entry point that succeeds clears the calling thread's pending text, so `dlerror()` describes the thread's most recent `dl*` call. (6) **Recursive `dlopen` (P-7):** an inner `dlopen` reaching an `Initialising` object returns its handle without running its constructors again. (7) **Handles (P-12):** a handle is the object's link map; `l_name` is the name as opened, `""` for the program. (8) **The program and system objects (P-13):** `dlopen` of the program by path is refused with the executable texts (`NOLOAD`: NULL without a text); `libc.so.6` by any name or path, and `ld.so` by its name or its `PT_INTERP` path, return the start-time object. Items (4) and (5) widen the plan text (ruling #5127, coordinator 2026-11-12: follow the reference). Not decided here (open maintainer rulings #5125 and #5126): whether P-10 (Liella runs no IFUNC resolver in a failing `dlopen`) and P-13 (`ld.so` by its real path returns the start-time object in Liella) become differences rows. |
| D-27.35 | §27.1 | — | **The dynamic-link mode of the conformance harness (DL-16H `CONF-DYN-HELPERS`).** A `conformance/c` program that names helpers (`LINK-HELPERS`: linked, `DLOPEN-HELPERS`: opened at run time; sources in `conformance/c/helpers/`, per-helper flags in `HELPER-FLAGS: <helper> <flags>`, `LINK-EXPORT-DYNAMIC` for `-rdynamic`) is built twice and run twice by `conformance/run.sh`: the reference's build (host compiler, host C library and loader) and Liella's (`-nodefaultlibs` against `target/liella/libc.so.6`, interpreter `target/liella/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2`). Both runs are judged by the same `EXPECT-*` directives, so a program states the probed behaviour once and the reference proves the program right before Liella is judged by it. **Helpers:** each helper's `.so` is removed before its build and checked to exist after it, in both sets; a helper that is missing, does not build or was not built fails the program, whichever run would have noticed. Programs get `CONF_HELPERS` and `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` set to their own helper directory. **Interim (until ld.so searches the run path):** Liella's builds link a copy of `libc.so.6` without `DT_SONAME` through a `libc.so` script (with the host's `libc_nonshared.a`), so the program reaches Liella's libc by path, as the `conformance_dynamic` product test does; when the library search lands, Liella's builds link `libc.so.6` by soname and the copy goes. **`PENDING-LIELLA: <story>`:** for behaviour Liella's loader does not have yet. The reference must pass; Liella's run failing prints `conformance: PENDING <program> on Liella until <story>` and counts as passed (the summary says how many were pending); Liella's run passing is a FAIL (drop the directive and the clause test's pending assertion); any build failure is a FAIL. A pending program links with `--unresolved-symbols=ignore-all`, so a missing export fails its run, not its link. Pending is not a skip: the clause tests assert the PENDING line by name (`s27_1_f_0`: `s27_dlopen_failures` until DL-16a; `s27_1_c_3`: `s27_dlsym_handles` until DL-16b), and the day the loader work lands the run fails until the mark is removed. **Reporting:** each run's misses name the run (`<program> (reference): ...`, `<program> (Liella): ...`) and its FAIL line names that run's stderr file (`conformance/build/<program>.log.ref.stderr` or `.log.liella.stderr`); `cargo xtask affected`'s report of a failed program (D-X.27) prefixes the ends with the run and tails that run's stdout and stderr. **Selection:** a file under `conformance/c/helpers/` selects every conformance program in `cargo xtask affected` (helpers and version maps are shared). Tests: `s27_1_f_0`, `s27_1_c_3` (crates/core/tests/s27_dynlink_clauses.rs); plants in handoff/CONF-DYN-HELPERS-plants.txt (a helper left unbuilt in either set, the pending verdict). |
| D-27.36 | §22.1, §22.6, §27.3 | — | **Threads with TLS in dynamically linked programs; TLS descriptors (DL-15 `DL-TLS-THREADS`, design §7, R14-8).** Under Liella's `ld.so`, `pthread_create` and `thrd_create` create threads: D-22.10's dynamic `EAGAIN` now applies only under another loader (or when the loader gives no TLS interface). **Interface:** the loader passes its per-thread TLS interface in `StartInfo` (the record `__liella_libc_early_init` receives, D-27.22) instead of the `LIELLA_PRIVATE` exports design §7/§14 named: `tls_size` (bytes a thread's static area needs below TP), `tls_align`, `tls_init(tp)` and `tls_release(tp)` as function addresses. Gain: `libc.so.6` gets no version need on `ld.so`'s private node, so it still loads under another loader (which never calls the early hook, so threads stay refused there), and no symbol lookup is involved; a mismatched pair is already refused by the build tag (D-27.22). The C library keeps it only when the size is non-zero, the alignment a power of two no larger than a page, and both hooks are set. **Layout:** a new thread's static area repeats the initial thread's (D-27.20): every initially loaded module's block at the same TP offset, the 64 KiB surplus, then the dtv in the lowest words of the area (`tls_size` = the initial area's bytes below TP + the dtv's words). The C library reserves it below TP in the thread's mapping (as the executable's block in a static program) and calls `tls_init` after writing the thread block, before the clone: each block gets its image and zeros to `p_memsz`, the dtv is built, and the block's dtv word points at it. A reused mapping's area below TP is no longer cleared by the C library (`tls_init` rewrites every block and the dtv; the surplus is left as it is). `tls_release` runs after the thread's destructors; the static area goes with the mapping, so it has nothing to release yet (the place for DL-19's dynamic blocks). **TLSDESC:** `R_X86_64_TLSDESC` is applied (no longer refused) as `[liella_machine_ld_tlsdesc_static, TP offset]` (`Arch::tls_descriptor`, the `TpOff` arithmetic; A. Oliva, "Thread-Local Storage Descriptors for IA32 and AMD64/EM64T", 2005), every initially loaded module being static; an image without a descriptor function still refuses it. `csys/src/machine/tlsdesc.S` holds the two fixed-name primitives with the register convention in its header: `_static` (`movq 8(%rax),%rax; ret`) and `_dynamic`, a branch-free trampoline for DL-19: its argument points at a record whose first word is a resolver `fn(record) -> address`; it saves rcx, rdx, rsi, rdi, r8-r11 and the FXSAVE state in a 64-byte aligned frame (any entry alignment), calls the resolver, subtracts `%fs:0` and restores. FXSAVE (not XSAVE) because the resolver is baseline SSE2 code, which leaves the upper ymm/zmm halves, zmm16-31 and the mask registers untouched; a resolver that uses AVX needs an XSAVE variant. Flags are not preserved (the convention's). Tests: `crates/boundary/tests/dl_tls_threads.rs` (`tlsdesc_functions_keep_every_register_but_rax`: both primitives forced by the caller, all registers, MXCSR and x87 control word, stack aligned and off by 8, a resolver that clobbers everything; `threads_get_static_tls_of_every_initial_module`: GD, LD, IE and TLSDESC in a library, LE in the program, threads from the program and the library, three rounds over reused mappings, per-thread `errno`, on the reference and on Liella through `PT_INTERP` and `ld.so PROGRAM`); `crates/ld/tests/tls.rs` (`tls_relocation_arithmetic_from_the_table`: the descriptor words). Plants: handoff/DL-TLS-THREADS-plants.txt. (Amended by D-27.39.) |
| D-27.37 | §27 | — | **`dlopen` in `ld.so`: loader state, refusal order and dlerror texts (phase 14 DL-16a, stories DL-DLOPEN-LOAD and -2; plan/ph14/dl-16-dlopen.md §1-§4; implements D-27.30, D-27.31, D-27.34).** (1) **State on first use:** the loader's state (object records, global scope, path and dependency arenas) lives in one private `MAP_NORESERVE` mapping made at the first `dlopen`, so a program that never calls it pays nothing; the start-time objects are described from their memory images (`image_view`), and the start records what that needs (program headers, bias, `(st_dev, st_ino)` per object; argc, argv, envp and auxv) without allocating. Capacity: 512 objects in the process and `init::OBJECTS_MAX` new objects per call; one more is refused with a dlerror text. (2) **Order of the checks per candidate file** (`liella_ld::dlopen::check`): the ELF header, the segments, the dynamic section, a position-independent executable, then static TLS (refused until DL-16d places it); the first failing check gives the text, each one the reference's text as probed (`spec/behaviour/dynlink.md`, "dlerror texts"). A header the reader refuses for a rule the reference does not check (`e_ehsize`, a `p_align` that is not a power of two) gives `malformed ELF object` (registered options for ruling #5294 in the pending records of this story). (3) **Mode:** every bit outside `RTLD_LAZY\|RTLD_NOW\|RTLD_NOLOAD\|RTLD_DEEPBIND\|RTLD_GLOBAL\|RTLD_NODELETE` is refused with `invalid mode parameter` before any search, and a mode with neither binding bit with `<file>: invalid mode for dlopen(): Invalid argument`; the test sweeps all 32 bits. This is the reference's behaviour (probe P-1), so it has no differences row. (4) **Texts:** `<name as given>: <reason>`, or the reason alone where the reference gives no name (a missing dependency names the dependency), composed into the calling thread's record (D-27.2) and cut to the record's size. (5) **Constructors** of a new set run after the loader's exclusive borrow of its state ends, under the re-entrant writer lock (D-27.30), so a constructor's own `dlopen` (probe P-7) works; the open count saturates at `u32::MAX` and pins the object. (6) **Identity:** a bare name is matched against `DT_SONAME` first, a found file by `(st_dev, st_ino)` (D-27.34 item 2); `ld.so` by any path is the start-time object (ruling #5126, registered option in this story's pending records). Tests: `crates/ld/tests/dlopen.rs` (`s27_1_c_1_dlopen_loads_and_refuses_with_texts`), `crates/boundary/src/dlerr.rs` (`s27_1_c_5_compose_concatenates_and_cuts_before_the_nul`), `crates/ld/tests/elf_reader.rs` (`bad_ehsize`, `bad_align`). |
| D-27.38 | §22.1, §27.3 | — | **The loader's per-thread TLS rides on the static TLS image word; one signal-mask call per thread creation (DL-TLS-THREADS-COST, fix forward of ruling #5285).** `set_loader_tls` stores the area Liella's `ld.so` reserves below TP as the thread TLS image with address 0 (`TLS_IMAGE`), and its `tls_init` / `tls_release` in two words of their own. `pthread_create` reads one image (size word first: a program without TLS reads one word) and in that image's branch either copies it or, for address 0, calls `tls_init` (before the thread block's stores, none of which touches the dtv word it writes). A reused mapping is cleared from the TLS block as for a static program, so under Liella's `ld.so` the surplus of a reused mapping is zero like a fresh one's. The creator's mask comes from the `sigprocmask` call that blocks every signal for the clone (its old mask), not from a separate query; the mask is restored only when blocking succeeded. Together they bring static `pthread_create` + `pthread_join` back to or below its count before DL-TLS-THREADS (`validation/wl_percall.sh`, instructions:u; numbers in handoff/DL-TLS-THREADS-COST.md), with the exit path's `tls_release` check kept. Local, testable detail; no interface change. |
| D-27.39 | §27.1, §27.3 | — | **`dlopen` of objects with `PT_TLS`: blocks in the static surplus (DL-16d `DL-DLOPEN-TLS-SURPLUS`, plan/ph14/dl-16-dlopen.md §5, R14-4).** `dlopen` no longer refuses an object with `PT_TLS`. **Place:** after the version check and before relocation (its `TPOFF`/`DTPMOD`/`TLSDESC` values need it), each new object with TLS gets the next module ID and a place in the 64 KiB surplus below every thread pointer (`liella_ld::tls::Surplus`): first fit nearest the thread pointer, keeping the block's alignment and its `p_vaddr` remainder; an alignment above the thread pointer's, no room, or no module slot left fails with `<path>: cannot allocate memory in static TLS block` (the probed text; dynamic blocks are DL-19's). A failed `dlopen` gives its places back (`unwind`). Places are never freed before DL-17. The start objects' `Obj.tls` is now their initial place, so a `dlopen`ed object's TLS relocation against a start object's symbol resolves. **One lock, the C library's thread-list lock:** `pthread_create` runs the loader's `tls_init` inside the same critical section that lists the new thread (the list insert's body is inlined there; `list_insert` stays for the initial thread), chosen by the loader's hook word, which is non-zero exactly when the image address is 0 (Liella's `ld.so` owns the area; both are set once at start-up). A static program's image copy stays before the descriptor stores, outside the lock (no static program loads TLS with `dlopen`), so nothing is kept live across the descriptor setup; the static path pays one compare. The two start words of a new thread (and of `clone`) are stored with straight-line code (`conv::store_words` takes a fixed-size array), which more than pays for it: static `thread_create_join` 35940.2 instructions per call on the base, 35922.2 here (wl_percall, release products, Haswell host, sd 0). Before publishing the new objects, `dlopen` (loader lock held; order loader lock, then thread-list lock) calls the C library's `LIELLA_PRIVATE` export `__liella_thread_walk(cb, ctx)`: under the thread-list lock, `cb(ctx, tp)` for each listed thread (and the caller if unlisted), then `cb(ctx, 0)`. The loader's callback writes each new block (image, then zeros to `p_memsz`) and the thread's dtv slots, count and generation; on 0 it appends the modules to the table later `tls_init` calls read and moves the generation on. A racing creation therefore reads the table either before the walk (and is listed for it) or after it, and gets each new block exactly once; threads created later get every module. The walk is looked up only by the first `dlopen` that loads TLS (no start-up cost); without it the open fails with the same text. **Capacity:** the module table holds 512 entries (`MODULES_MAX`) and every dtv has room for 512 module slots, reserved as address space (only the header and the used slots are written), so a slot never moves. **dtv:** eager for live threads (the walk); `__tls_get_addr`'s slow path, entered when a thread's generation differs from the current one, rewrites every slot from the table, then the count and the generation (a thread whose vector fell behind repairs it; a module the table does not hold aborts, §27.3 Failure). Gain over a lazily allocated block per thread: no allocation and no failure path on first access, the initial-exec and TLS-descriptor accesses use the static return, and no per-access cost for programs that never `dlopen` TLS. `dlsym` of an `STT_TLS` symbol in a `dlopen`ed object (DL-16b) is not on next yet: the table is the place its answer comes from. Tests: `conformance/c/s27_dlopen_tls_surplus.c` (`s27_3_c_0`: GD, LD, IE and TLSDESC in `dlopen`ed objects from threads created before, after and during the `dlopen`, a relocation against the program's TLS, the exhaustion text, 80 failed opens giving their place back), `crates/ld/tests/tls.rs` (`tls_surplus_first_fit_alignment_gap_reuse_and_rollback`). Plants: handoff/DL-DLOPEN-TLS-SURPLUS-plants.txt. |
| D-27.40 | §27.1 | — | **The eight high `dlopen` mode bits are internal to glibc and unsupported in Liella (DLOPEN-INTERNAL-BITS; owner ruling DLOPEN INTERNAL MODE BITS, 2026-11-13).** glibc's maintainers confirmed that `0x01000000`, `0x02000000`, `0x04000000`, `0x08000000`, `0x10000000`, `0x20000000`, `0x40000000` (used internally for profiling) and `0x80000000` are internal, undocumented flags and suggested leaving them out of any analysis. **The eight bits are reserved for Liella** (owner ruling, 2026-11-13): Liella owes glibc's internal meaning of them nothing, refuses them today with `invalid mode parameter`, and keeps them available for a possible future Liella-defined use (none planned; any use is a new public-interface decision). **Rule:** Liella's behaviour is unchanged: `dlopen` refuses every bit outside `RTLD_LAZY`, `RTLD_NOW`, `RTLD_NOLOAD`, `RTLD_DEEPBIND`, `RTLD_GLOBAL`, `RTLD_NODELETE` with `invalid mode parameter` before the file is looked for (`ModeError::Unknown`), and DL-16a's sweep test keeps asserting it for every undefined bit, these eight included. They are excluded from the comparison with the reference: probe P-1's sweep (`tools/probe/dl/dlopen/probe.c`) skips all eight and no longer probes `0x80000000` alone; the existing raw lines in `spec/behaviour/dynlink.glibc.txt` stay. **Record:** `spec/behaviour/dynlink.md` row "P-1 unknown bits" and one row in `docs/differences-from-glibc.md`. No compatibility option: they are not a public interface (owner ruling). |
| D-27.41 | §27 | — | **`dlsym` and `dlvsym` in `ld.so` (phase 14 DL-16b, stories DL-DLSYM and -2; plan/ph14/dl-16-dlopen.md §2 and §8; spec/behaviour/dynlink.md "Symbol binding", probes P-3..P-6; owner ruling #5127; coordinator ruling #5264; implements D-27.32).** (1) **Entry:** libc.so.6 exports `dlsym` and `dlvsym` (`GLIBC_2.34`, with the `GLIBC_2.2.5` compatibility aliases); a frame-free entry passes the caller's return address to the loader's `dlsym` through `StartInfo`. libc.a's entries fail with NULL and the text `dlsym: no symbols can be looked up in a statically linked program` (or `dlvsym: ...`), never a crash (D-27.33, #5264). (2) **Scopes:** `RTLD_DEFAULT` searches the global scope, then, for a caller loaded by `dlopen`, the local scope it was relocated with, objects not already searched (#5127, P-5); `RTLD_NEXT` searches the objects after the caller in the scope it was loaded with (the global scope for a start-time caller, its root's local scope for a `dlopen`ed one); a handle searches its object's local scope (itself, then its dependencies breadth-first); the program's handle (`dlopen(NULL)`) searches the global scope. `RTLD_DEEPBIND` puts an object's local scope before the global scope in its own relocations, each object once. (3) **Answers:** `dlsym` accepts a base or default definition and `dlvsym` exactly the named version (D-27.11 as amended by this story's second record); an `STB_GNU_UNIQUE` definition goes through the namespace's unique table (an entry there, else the start's binding: the first unique definition in the start's global scope), and the answer pins its definer (`nodelete`); an IFUNC answers its resolver's result, the resolver called after the loader's borrow ends; an `STT_TLS` symbol of a start-time object answers the calling thread's address (thread pointer + the object's static TLS offset + the symbol's value). (4) **Handles** are checked by one range test over the object records (D-27.32); anything else is refused with `dlsym: invalid handle` (`dlvsym: invalid handle`) and never dereferenced. (5) **Texts:** `<object>: undefined symbol: <name>[, version <v>]`, the object being the handle's, or the caller's for the special handles (the program by `argv[0]`, a start-time object by its path, a `dlopen`ed one by the path it was opened with); a successful call clears the calling thread's pending text (#5127). (6) **Lock:** the call takes the loader's re-entrant writer lock (a constructor may call `dlsym`; a unique binding records a table entry) until DL-16c gives lookups lock-free readers (plan §4). Measured: no instruction-count row covers `dlsym` yet; no start-up code changed. |
| D-27.42 | §27 | — | **A named version (`dlvsym`) never matches in an object without version tables (amends D-27.11; phase 14 DL-16b; spec/behaviour/dynlink.md, "`dlvsym` missing version ... also for an object without versions").** D-27.11 let every definition of an object without `versym` match every request. That stays for relocations: an unversioned reference, a lookup by name alone (`dlsym`) and a relocation's versioned reference still bind such a definition (the load-time version check refuses a program that needs a version from such an object, ruling #3655). A named-version request (`dlvsym`, and the unique table's lookup of a definition's own version) now matches only a definition of exactly that version, so in an object without `versym` (each definition reads as base, index 1) it matches nothing and the scope search goes on to the next object; when nothing matches, the call fails with `<object>: undefined symbol: <name>, version <v>`, as the probed reference does. |

| D-29.1 | §29 | HIST, COMPAT | RPC and XDR follow RFC 5531/4506. NIS follows the YP protocol. STREAMS and removed interfaces are `ENOSYS` stubs. `_IO_*` vtable objects export tables of our functions (F32). |
| D-29.2 | §29.1 | COMPAT | **UDP RPC replies from the called address only** (owner ruling 2026-10-23, #1643, provisional): the UDP client compares each datagram's `recvfrom` source (port and IPv4 address) with the called address and drops any other, whatever its xid; the socket is not connected (that would change ICMP error reporting). A reply-shaped datagram (type REPLY, status accepted or denied; the xid is never consulted) from another address during a call turns its timeout into `RPC_CANTRECV` with `EREMCHG`; nothing ends a call early. Each call's xid is fresh random bits (`getrandom`), except the call after `CLSET_XID`, which is stepped from the set value as probed. Opt-out COMPAT-12 (`liella.compat.rpc_reply_any_source=1`, ignored when `AT_SECURE`). `clnt_broadcast` and TCP are not affected. Reason: replies over UDP are matched by xid only; accepting them from any source lets a third party who can send packets to the client answer in the server's place. **Superseded by D-29.5** (the UDP client is a failing stub; COMPAT-12 withdrawn). |
| D-29.3 | §29.4 | COMPAT | **`<regexp.h>` `step`/`advance` are stubs; `malloc_get_state`/`malloc_set_state` stay failing stubs** (owner rulings R6 and R9, 2026-11-04, SCOPE-APPLY-STUBS). `step` and `advance` return 0 (no match) for every argument and never write `loc1`, `loc2` or `locs`; the three objects stay exported, so old binaries still link. LG-10 (the matcher) is deferred until the LG-19 corpus finds a user. `malloc_get_state` returns NULL and `malloc_set_state` returns -1, both with `errno` ENOSYS (D-3.5, unchanged); `mtrace`/`muntrace` are unchanged. No compatibility option: the interfaces are obsolete and the old matcher is not offered (recorded in the differences row). |

Failure table: `ecb_crypt`/`cbc_crypt` `DESERR_HWERROR` (2), buffer untouched; `des_setparity` no effect; `passwd2des` no effect (key untouched); `xencrypt`/`xdecrypt`, `key_secretkey_is_set`, `getpublickey`, `getsecretkey`, `authdes_getucred`, `user2netname`, `host2netname`, `getnetname`, `netname2user`, `netname2host` `0`; `key_setsecret`, `key_gendes`, `key_encryptsession[_pk]`, `key_decryptsession[_pk]`, `key_get_conv`, `key_setnet` `-1`; `authdes_create`, `authdes_pk_create`, `authunix_create[_default]` `NULL`. Every stub sets `errno` to `EOPNOTSUPP` and touches no network, file or key server. Test: `crates/boundary/tests/s29_rpc_auth_stubs.rs`.
